<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/eastern-canada__011.html" data-result-title="Eastern Canada — 33rd (2005) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Eastern Canada</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>33rd (2005)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Eastern Canada" href="../rpr/exc/eastern-canada__011.html">Eastern Canada</a><p class="rpr-card__body">No record of previous experience approved as internship fulfilling the “full range of ministerial duties” nor is there record of ¾ vote of presbytery to approve equivalency internship. BCO 19-16 Response : The Presbytery of Eastern Canada confesses with chagrin that it had not noted the requirement of BCO 19-16 for a ¾ majority to approve previous experience as equivalent to internship. We will try to better in the future. We remember no dissenting vote to this action, so it should not be considered invalid, though it was not properly done. However, nothing in the BCO or RAO requires us to record that a candidate has fulfilled the “full range of ministerial duties”, but only to ensure that he has. We have never made such a statement in our minutes. In the case cited, the report from [name omitted] Presbyterian Church session was clear to that effect, and we indicated that this was accomplished by agreeing that he had “ sufficiently completed the requirements for internship’ [emphasis added].</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/eastern-canada.html">Eastern Canada</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/westminster__031.html" data-result-title="Westminster — 41st (2013) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Westminster</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>41st (2013)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Westminster" href="../rpr/exc/westminster__031.html">Westminster</a><p class="rpr-card__body">No record of approval of call and Ordination of TE: terms of call not included (also BCO 13-11, “full and accurate record”). Response: July 14, 2012; October 13, 2012 . In our Manual, our presbytery has authorized the shepherding committee as a commission to handle the dissolution and transfer of Teaching Elders as long as everything is in order and there is no objection by the congregation or the Pastor. They simply report their actions to the court. Such was the case with the actions taken at the July meeting of presbytery. TE [name omitted] was without call, and TE [name omitted] was approved and it was reported (page 7/Shepherding Committee/rec 2-3). These matters will be recorded in the future. Excerpt from Presbytery Manual: The Committee(Shepherding) shall have the power to constitute itself as a commission in order to facilitate the transfer of a teaching elder to another presbytery when all the provisions required in BCO 23-1 have been fulfilled and there is compliance on both the part of the congregation and the pastor. This power is granted in order to expedite a transfer between stated meetings of presbytery when both the pastor and the congregation have mutually agreed to the dissolution.</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/westminster.html">Westminster</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/southern-louisiana__006.html" data-result-title="Southern Louisiana — 43rd (2015) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Southern Louisiana</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>43rd (2015)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Southern Louisiana" href="../rpr/exc/southern-louisiana__006.html">Southern Louisiana</a><p class="rpr-card__body">- Approval for TE to serve out of bounds with inadequate documentation, i.e., no assurance in the written call to allow “full freedom to maintain and teach the doctrines of the church.” Response : Presbytery agrees with the exception. ( BCO 20-1 and BCO 8-7) are clear that the Presbytery is to be assured that teaching elders laboring out bounds are afforded the “full freedom to maintain and teach the doctrines of the church.” SLAP wrongfully assumed TE [Name Omitted] would be afforded such freedom based on the relationships that exist between many of our members and missionaries working with the Christian Missionary Society in Peru and based on previous work experience and partnerships our members have had with this Society. We realize this is insufficient to merit the “assurance” required of our constitution. In response, we have requested and received written assurances from the Christian Missionary Society of Peru and the local church where TE [Name Omitted] is serving. We apologize for this oversight and promise to be more careful in the future</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/southern-louisiana.html">Southern Louisiana</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/korean-southeastern__004.html" data-result-title="Korean Southeastern — 23rd (1995) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Korean Southeastern</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>23rd (1995)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Korean Southeastern" href="../rpr/exc/korean-southeastern__004.html">Korean Southeastern</a><p class="rpr-card__body">There is no record of examination for a man licensed (BCO 19-2), and for a TE admitted (BCO 13-6). July 15,1993; December 12,1994; March 10,1995: There is no record that the call for the meeting was approved (BCO 13-11). July 15, 1993, p. 3: There is no record that a pastor&#x27;s call was approved by Presbytery. (BCO 21-1). April 11-12,1994, p. 1: there is no record of a call for a TE admitted to Presbytery (BCO 21-1). June 20-21, 1994, p. 2: There is no record of a congregational meeting concerning pastor&#x27;s resignation (BCO 23-1). December 12, 1994, p. 3: The proposed Council (or Association) of Korean Presbyteries is not authorized by BCO 13-9 in responsibilities of presbyteries, without permission of GA; nor is it permissible for these presbyteries to meet for business while the GA is in session without the Assembly&#x27;s approval. NOTE: While there is no objection to the Korean Commissioners meeting for fellowship at GA, the CRPR is concerned with the possibility of the formation of a synodical body which would assume some of the responsibilities of the GA, and tend to separate more than integrate the KLPs within the PCA. Adopted</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/korean-southeastern.html">Korean Southeastern</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> raised (open)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/new-jersey__014.html" data-result-title="New Jersey — 30th (2002) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">New Jersey</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>30th (2002)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="New Jersey" href="../rpr/exc/new-jersey__014.html">New Jersey</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Incomplete exams. RAO 14-3e.5 ; BCO 21-4 Response submitted to the 31 [st] GA: Presbytery respectfully disagrees with the interpretation of the standards, RAO 14-3e.5; BCO 21-4 (The candidates in question each came fully meeting the standards of BCO 21-4.) Presbytery recognizes the words of RAO 143e.5. It believes that the form recorded in its minutes, “… in all respects in accord with BCO 13-6…” is tantamount to listing each item individually. As support for this interpretation, Presbytery cites a previous incident. The exception to Presbytery’s minutes for 1996 cites a failure to list required details. Presbytery’s response was, “the minutes indicate that the candidate was received in accordance with BCO 18-2 and 18-3.” The minutes of Presbytery’s September 1998 meeting, under the listing of correspondence received, indicate that the Clerk of the General Assembly reported that New Jersey’s minutes were approved. Thus a previous vote of the General Assembly has approved Presbytery’s interpretation. Response submitted to the 32 [nd] GA: We will challenge no further the difference of opinion between NJ Presbytery and the Review Committee and record our examinations processes in the future as the committee requests. 32 [nd] GA Note: General Assembly reminds the presbytery that the difference was between GA and the presbytery, not the Review Committee. Adopted</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/new-jersey.html">New Jersey</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

Missouri Presbytery does accept a seminary degree in lieu of an oral examination in the original language according to BCO 21-4-a, however, this was not recorded in the minutes. The clerk will make the necessary changes and endeavor to include this information in future minutes. Examination in the area of PCA history has been included in the clerk’s recording of the examination in Church History. The clerk will make the necessary changes and endeavor to make specific mention of examination in PCA history in future minutes. All men examined were required to submit theological/exegetical papers according to BCO 21-4 as well. The clerk failed to record the receipt and approval of such exams and will make the necessary changes and endeavor to record this information in future minutes. Adopted</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/missouri.html">Missouri</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/northern-illinois__043.html" data-result-title="Northern Illinois — 34th (2006) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Northern Illinois</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>34th (2006)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Northern Illinois" href="../rpr/exc/northern-illinois__043.html">Northern Illinois</a><p class="rpr-card__body">: No record of examination for ordination BCO 21-4, RAO 14-3.e.5. Response : We acknowledge that the minutes may be confusing since they do not reflect information included in previous minutes. When TE T— transferred into the Presbytery of Northern Illinois (Stated Meeting, July 23, 2002), he was examined by the presbytery then to serve as a church planter in the Rogers Park neighborhood area of Chicago. A commission was formed to install TE T— at that meeting. Thanks. Rationale : The exception does not refer to the TE mentioned in the response. Only one man was examined for ordination at the April 1112 2005, meeting (05 - 26 Candidates and Credentials Committee Report) and this is not the same man referred to in the response. Response : The record shows in paragraph 05-26 that Mr. T—, a licentiate with the presbytery, was being examined for ordination, in order to accept a call to plant a church. However, what is recorded in the minutes is an incomplete ordination examination (the record reflects he was examined in Christian experience, motives for seeking the ministry, church history, sacraments, and the History of the PCA). We remember this examination being a complete examination as required by the Book of Church Order . We will ensure that we include in the record all elements of future examinations. Thanks.</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/northern-illinois.html">Northern Illinois</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/evangel__039.html" data-result-title="Evangel — 35th (2007) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Evangel</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>35th (2007)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Evangel" href="../rpr/exc/evangel__039.html">Evangel</a><p class="rpr-card__body">October 25, 2006 : No record of specific examination requirements. BCO 21-4. Response : To the exceptions taken to the minutes of the Feb. 14 [th], May 9 [th], and August 8 [th] 2006 Presbytery meetings concerning the lack of any record of specific examinations requirements having been met by both candidates and licentiates, The following responses were approved at the 117 [th] meeting of Evangel Presbytery (2-12-2008): “In all three set of Minutes referred to, the language used for each candidate was, ‘…upon his examination.’ It was only recorded that each candidate was, ‘…examined for the credentials required of a candidate’ and ‘after discussion the examinations were sustained.’ This language was in error. This Presbytery gratefully acknowledges the discovery of this error and assures the General Assembly through its Review of Presbytery Records Committee that all of the men in question met the requirements of BCO 18-1 through 18-3. The proper language will in the future be carefully examined to insure that the proper procedures are properly reported.” “It is also acknowledged that there have been lapses in specifically recording the details of the examinations in several other instances in our Minutes, namely the lack of records concerning internships. These lapses were just that – lapses. We will redouble our efforts to report fully on this very important work of the Presbytery regarding examinations. We are grateful to the Assembly for its forbearance as we adjust our reporting to meet expectations.” Adopted</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/evangel.html">Evangel</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/eastern-canada__013.html" data-result-title="Eastern Canada — 37th (2009) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Eastern Canada</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>37th (2009)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Eastern Canada" href="../rpr/exc/eastern-canada__013.html">Eastern Canada</a><p class="rpr-card__body">All specific requirements of ordination exam not recorded Response : That we amend the minutes page 570 by inserting, “Since this completes the required exam for ordination (Minutes, pp. 565, 566),” as a clause before the recommendation that [name omitted] be ordained, to read: “Since this completes the required exam for ordination (Minutes, pp.565, 566), Recommended that [name omitted] be ordained by Presbytery in view of the call received from the session of Westminster BPC” That we answer in these terms: “The Presbytery of Eastern Canada reports that it was difficult to record all the requirements for an ordination exam October 17, 2008, since we did not examine anybody on that date. However, we assume RPR’s reference is actually to the conclusion of an examination February 29, 2008. Presbytery assures the General Assembly that all requirements for the exam were duly recorded when they took place (Minutes pp. 565, 566, 570). All but the two items recorded on page 570 took place in the previous meeting, in 2007. For clarity we have inserted an amendment in our minutes of February 29, 2008 to refer to the rest of the examination at the previous meeting.”</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/eastern-canada.html">Eastern Canada</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/susquehanna-valley__019.html" data-result-title="Susquehanna Valley — 39th (2011) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Susquehanna Valley</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>39th (2011)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Susquehanna Valley" href="../rpr/exc/susquehanna-valley__019.html">Susquehanna Valley</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Not all required elements of ordination exam included in the minutes. Minority Report on Recommendation c [second Exception of Substance] for Susquehanna Valley by a vote of 29-22, the RPR committee adopted a recommendation to cite Susquehanna Valley Presbytery with an exception of substance for sustaining a BCO 13-6 transfer exam of a PCA minister who expressed a difference with Larger Catechism 177 and his view, but not practice, on the admissibility of covenant children to the Lord’s Supper. The Minority intends to recommend the General Assembly not cite Susquehanna Valley with an exception of substance for their judgment on this matter. The following 18 men indicated their intent to present a Minority Report. A more extensive Minority Report may be posted later. TE Dan Adamson Chicago Metro TE John Barrett Savannah River TE Kirk Blankenship Piedmont Triad RE Richard Dolan Georgia Foothills RE Howie Donahoe Pacific Northwest TE Bobbie Griffith North Texas TE Todd Gwennap Eastern Carolina TE Dan Herron Central Indiana TE Bradley Jones Western Canada TE Dan Kaiser Pacific TE Kevin Labby Central Florida TE Tim LeCroy Missouri TE Dave Lindberg Metro Atlanta TE Patrick Morgan Siouxlands TE Erik Swanson Metro New York TE Paul Warren Chesapeake TE Tim Weldon Gulfstream TE Sam Wheatley Northern California</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/susquehanna-valley.html">Susquehanna Valley</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>
<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/western-canada__008.html" data-result-title="Western Canada — 39th (2011) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Western Canada</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>39th (2011)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Western Canada" href="../rpr/exc/western-canada__008.html">Western Canada</a><p class="rpr-card__body">No indication of candidate’s knowledge of original languages Response: Presbytery agrees with the exception because the minutes were not as clear as they should have been. The candidate in question completed both Hebrew and Greek on-line studies, Greek through RTS Virtual, and Hebrew through Associated Mennonite Biblical Seminary, Elkhart, Indiana, plus mentorship by a TE of this Presbytery. These studies, including the mentorship, were approved by the Credentials Committee, and accepted by Presbytery in lieu of examination. Presbytery will add a clarifying note to its minutes to reflect the above. For the RPR Committee’s information, Presbytery also passed the following additional recommendation, giving the clarifying information to correct our minutes on this matter. Recommendation: That Presbytery clarify its minutes of Oct. 2, 2010, by adding, “Mr. completed both Hebrew and Greek on-line studies, Greek through RTS Virtual, and Hebrew through Associated Mennonite Biblical Seminary, Elkhart, Indiana, plus mentorship by TE , and these studies, including the mentorship, were approved by the Credentials Committee.”</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/western-canada.html">Western Canada</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/palmetto__026.html" data-result-title="Palmetto — 43rd (2015) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Palmetto</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>43rd (2015)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Palmetto" href="../rpr/exc/palmetto__026.html">Palmetto</a><p class="rpr-card__body">April 28, 2011 and July 28, 2011 ( BCO 21-4) - No record of exam in PCA history. Response : Examinations of candidates for ordination in Palmetto Presbytery do include an examination in PCA history before the committee and before Presbytery. as far as we remember, the exam of [Name Omitted] (April 28, 2011) did include the area of PCA history. Palmetto Presbytery does apologize for not including this specific detail in its minutes. In the exams of [Name Omitted] and [Name Omitted](July 28, 2011), two men who had been previously ordained and were transferring in from other PCA presbyteries, the Candidates Committee and the Presbytery followed the wording in ( BCO 13-6) which says, “Ministers seeking admission to a Presbytery from other Presbyteries in the PCA shall be examined on Christian experience, and also touching their views in theology, the Sacraments, and church government.” It had not been the understanding of Palmetto Presbytery that men who were previously ordained in the PCA. had to be examined in PCA History. we ask to be instructed if this interpretation is incorrect, so that we will change in this regard. The examination for ordination of [name omitted] did include PCA History.</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/palmetto.html">Palmetto</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/korean-central__082.html" data-result-title="Korean Central — 46th (2018) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Korean Central</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>46th (2018)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Korean Central" href="../rpr/exc/korean-central__082.html">Korean Central</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Ordination examination approved conditionally. Response [2018] : KCP disagrees with this exception. BCO 21-4 does not forbid a conditional approval of an ordination examination. Concerning the candidate in question, we checked his qualifications and examined the candidate with the subject matter prescribed in BCO 21-4.c. He affirmed our confessional standards with any exception. KCP’s examination committee was satisfied with the result of his examination. However, during the floor test, a few presbytery members were concerned that the candidate’s explanations on some of the issues concerning sexuality and the ordination of women seemed lacking. He affirmed our position, but a few members felt that he needed extra study on the matter. KCP could have ignored the minority concern, but KCP usually tries to satisfy all of its members. Therefore, KCP decided to approve of the candidate with an instruction to write papers (2-3 pages each) concerning the two topics of sexuality and the ordination of women. KCP took a vote and it was unanimous.</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/korean-central.html">Korean Central</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/central-florida__080.html" data-result-title="Central Florida — 47th (2019) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Central Florida</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>47th (2019)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Central Florida" href="../rpr/exc/central-florida__080.html">Central Florida</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Stated differences not recorded in candidate’s own words. Response : We agree. The following action was approved by the 173 [rd] Presbytery; “Move that the 168 [th] minutes be amended by inserting the following under TE Chuck Berry’s examination: My exception to the Westminster Confession of Faith is regarding the recreation clause in WCF 21:8, which states that on the Sabbath, people are to &quot;observe a holy rest, all the day, from their own works, words, and thoughts about their worldly employments and recreations…&quot;. I hold to the view that prohibiting “recreations” on the Sabbath is excessively restrictive. It is clear from Scripture that God calls us to a weekly REST and prohibits ‘work’ on the Sabbath (Exodus 20:8- 11), except for works of mercy and goodness by Jesus’ own example (Matt 12:11-13), but it is not clear that ‘recreations’, which can be considered restorative ‘rest’ from our weekly, vocational work routines, is included in the biblical prohibition. As Jesus said, &quot;The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath&quot; (Mark 2:27).</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/central-florida.html">Central Florida</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/korean-central__104.html" data-result-title="Korean Central — 49th (2022) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Korean Central</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>49th (2022)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Korean Central" href="../rpr/exc/korean-central__104.html">Korean Central</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Stated differences not recorded in the candidate’s own words. Response : Korean Central Presbytery agrees with this exception. The candidate, [name omitted], had the following exception to the Westminster Standards: WCF 4.1: Six Days of Creation: I do not undermine or deny the historicity of creation. With the respect to the length of the “days,” I support the Analogical Day view. Genesis 1:1-2 starts with “in the beginning,” and it represents unknown length of beginning “day.” Therefore, our (human) workdays are different from God’s workdays. The Scripture does not provide a specific information to examine the specific length of the “day.” Analogical Day view claims that creation day sets the pattern of the work and rest. Therefore, the night and day description explains the pattern of the rest and the recovery from the work. We apologize for not recording this exception in the candidate’s own words, and we will be careful to do so in the future. We have corrected this omission in our minutes through a motion to amend something previously adopted at our October 2022 stated meeting. Note: The minutes from our April 2021 meeting note that the Presbytery judged that this stated difference was more than semantic, but “not out of accord with any fundamental of our system of doctrine” (p. 8). [Note from Stated Clerk: Due to time constraints, the motions to amend something previously adopted were postponed to our next stated meeting.]</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/korean-central.html">Korean Central</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/philadelphia__063.html" data-result-title="Philadelphia — 51st (2024) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Philadelphia</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>51st (2024)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Philadelphia" href="../rpr/exc/philadelphia__063.html">Philadelphia</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Licensure candidate stated that he disagrees with the “strictness” of the Westminster Standards’ view of the Sabbath but is not clear on what his stated difference is. WCF 21.8, WLC 117, 119 WSC 60, 61 “I take exception to WCF 21.8 in that I don’t think that Scripture requires as strict of an observance of the Sabbath as the confessions seem to portray. Taking Matthew 12 as exegetical support, Jesus healed, and told the healed to pick up and go home. Also, to carry the spirit of Mark 2:27, Sabbath should be focused on spiritual rest and corporate worship, not mere outward action. But of course the two affect each other. I take exception to the strictness of the confessions.”</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/philadelphia.html">Philadelphia</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/suncoast-florida__037.html" data-result-title="Suncoast Florida — 51st (2024) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Suncoast Florida</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>51st (2024)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Suncoast Florida" href="../rpr/exc/suncoast-florida__037.html">Suncoast Florida</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Candidate’s stated difference(s) not recorded. Response:Response: The candidate coming for ordination had been licensed at the previous Stated Meeting of Presbytery where his stated differences were adjudged “as more than semantic, but not striking at the vitals of the system of doctrine as set forth in the Westminster Confession of Faith and Catechisms.” A note was added to the February minutes that the candidate’s stated differences had not changed since he was licensed at the September 13, 2022 Stated Meeting. 1. WSC 60 states that on the Sabbath day we are to observe “a holy resting all that day, even from such worldly employments and recreations as are lawful on other days; and spending the whole time in the public and private exercises of God’s worship.” While I largely agree with the Westminster view of the Sabbath, I believe that lawful, restful recreational activities are permissible on the Sabbath day. 2. WLC 109, in discussing the Second Commandment, describes this command as forbidding “the making any representation of God, of all or of any of the three persons, either inwardly in our mind, or outwardly in any kind of image or likeness of any creature whatsoever.” I believe that the formation of certain images of the three persons of the Trinity in one’s mind is almost impossible to avoid, particularly as Jesus took on flesh as a human person, and the Holy Spirit is depicted variously as a dove, tongues of fire, etc. I don’t find images such as these to be particularly harmful in things like children’s books, granted that these images are not to be worshiped nor are they to be perceived as actual portrayals of the persons of the godhead.</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/suncoast-florida.html">Suncoast Florida</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/piedmont-triad__024.html" data-result-title="Piedmont Triad — 52nd (2025) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Piedmont Triad</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>52nd (2025)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Piedmont Triad" href="../rpr/exc/piedmont-triad__024.html">Piedmont Triad</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Presbytery incorrectly judged a candidate’s stated difference as merely semantic. <article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/piedmont-triad__025.html" data-result-title="Piedmont Triad — 52nd (2025) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Piedmont Triad</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>52nd (2025)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Piedmont Triad" href="../rpr/exc/piedmont-triad__025.html">Piedmont Triad</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Presbytery incorrectly judged a candidate’s stated differences as merely semantic. First minute read: “I have a perceived difference with the WCF 4.1 (cf. also WLC 15; WSC 9) which states: “It pleased God the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost, for the manifestation of the glory of His eternal power, wisdom, and goodness, in the beginning, to create or make of nothing the world, and all things therein, whether visible or invisible, in the space of six days, and all very good.” The Confession here appears to teach that creation took place in the span of six, literal 24 hour periods. I do not believe an orthodox view of creation necessitates the “Calendar Day Interpretation” of Genesis 1-2. That being said, I believe God called all things, both invisible and visible, out of nothing (ex nihilo) into being by his voice, as the Belgic Confession 12 states without reference to the span of time: “We believe that the Father, when it seemed good to him, created heaven and earth and all other creatures from nothing, by the Word—that is to say, by the Son.” Second minute reads: “I have a perceived difference with the WCF 21.8 (cf. also WLC 1117, 119; WSC 60), which states: “This Sabbath is to be kept holy unto the Lord when men, after a due preparing of their hearts, and ordering of their common affairs beforehand, do not only observe an holy rest all the day from their own works, words, and thoughts about their worldly employments and recreations; but also are taken up the whole time in the public and private exercises of His worship, and in the duties of necessity and mercy.” The Confession here appears to teach that personal, private activities for pleasure are not appropriate on the Sabbath. I believe that New Covenant Christians keep the Sabbath holy primarily by worshiping God weekly on the First Day (i.e. Sunday). We rest from our work and ordinary labors in order to facilitate our worship of God. Recreational activities that do not hinder our ability to worship are still permissible. This view is expressed in the Heidelberg Catechism 103: “Q. What is God’s will for you in the fourth commandment? A. First, that the gospel ministry and education for it be maintained, and that, especially on the festive day of rest, I diligently attend the assembly of God’s people to learn what God’s Word teaches, to participate in the sacraments, to pray to God publicly, and to bring Christian offerings for the poor.”” Both statements depart from the Standards’ teaching on the relevant topics, and thus are more than semantic.</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/piedmont-triad.html">Piedmont Triad</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> raised (open)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>
<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/piedmont-triad__026.html" data-result-title="Piedmont Triad — 52nd (2025) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Piedmont Triad</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>52nd (2025)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Piedmont Triad" href="../rpr/exc/piedmont-triad__026.html">Piedmont Triad</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Presbytery incorrectly judged a candidate’s stated differences as merely semantic. Both stated differences actually differ from the Confession of Faith. The first difference reads: “I have a perceived difference with the WCF Chapter 21, Section 8: “The Sabbath is then kept holy unto the Lord, when men, after a due preparing of their hearts, and ordering of their affairs beforehand, do not only observe an holy rest, all the day, from their own, works, words, and thoughts about their worldly employments, and recreations, but also are taken up the whole time, in the public and private exercises of his worship, and in the duties of necessity, and mercy.” though i do believe it is important to keep the Sabbath as the Lord’s Day and to worship on the first day of the week, when Christ rose. As the pattern laid out in scripture. I do not think we have to literally rest from all worldly matters to keep this. As humans, we are to set aside a day of the week to worship and rest in the Lord. I think the proper way to observe the Sabbath day is to gather together as the body and worship our God and King. (Matt. 28, Acts 2) I do think it is important to set aside the Lord’s Day to be purposeful in your reflection on God and gather with the body in your local church. This way you hear the Word proclaimed, pray/reflect on the week. And partake of the Lord’s Supper in order to nourish your faith. Though I do not think per the confession, you can do nothing on the Sabbath. I do think doing things with your family, recreation, yardwork, etc. can all be means of rest and bring glory to God. This is part of our living our lives daily as Christians seeking to honor and serve Christ daily. In other words, as Christians we shouldn’t only think about Christ and his word on Sunday. Rather we are to live our daily lives praising him and serving him daily in our various callings. The Sabbath is the day set aside to prepare to live out this calling.” The second difference reads: “I have perceived difference with WCF chapter 4 section 1: “It pleased God the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost, and for the manifestation of the glory of his eternal power, wisdom, and goodness in the beginning, to create, or make of nothing, the world, and all things therein whether visible or invisible, in the space of six days; and all very good.” My view of creation would be the standard day age view. The ‘six days’ are understood in the same sense as “in that day” of Isaiah 11:10-11 —that is, as periods of indefinite length and not necessarily of 24 hours duration. There are other similar uses of the Hebrew word for “day” (yôm) in Scripture to support this view of periods longer than 24 hours including that in the very context of Genesis 2:4. Another argument for this approach is that the seventh day in Genesis 1 is not concluded with the boundary phrase, “and there was evening, and there was morning” as with the other days, and therefore it continues, as indicated by Hebrews 4:1-11&#x27;s quotation of Psalm 95:11.”</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/piedmont-triad.html">Piedmont Triad</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> raised (open)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/tennessee-valley__036.html" data-result-title="Tennessee Valley — 34th (2006) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Tennessee Valley</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>34th (2006)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Tennessee Valley" href="../rpr/exc/tennessee-valley__036.html">Tennessee Valley</a><p class="rpr-card__body">[name]’s examination recorded in terms of licensure exams instead of ordination. Unclear if he was properly examined for ordination. No record of questioning of exceptions to Standards. BCO 21-04, RAO 14-3.e.5.</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/tennessee-valley.html">Tennessee Valley</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>
<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/new-jersey__037.html" data-result-title="New Jersey — 46th (2018) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">New Jersey</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>46th (2018)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="New Jersey" href="../rpr/exc/new-jersey__037.html">New Jersey</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Use of extraordinary clause not explained. Actual 3/4 vote not recorded. Response : Upon further reflection, we believe we have erred in examining the man seeking to transfer into the PCA from the Presbyterian Church of Brazil, with whom the PCA has fraternal relations. We misinterpreted the language of BCO 13-6 to allow for us to use the extraordinary clause from BCO 21-4 to examine him according to views only, as if he were coming from another Presbytery. We did this because of his years of experience and training. The Presbytery vote was unanimous to use the extraordinary clause in this way (though not recorded in our minutes). However, in looking a tit more closely, the language of BCO 13-6 requires (shall) that a man coming from another denomination be examined in all areas according to BCO 21-4 (knowledge and views). We could have used the extraordinary clause at that time to omit parts of the examination based on his many years of experience in the Presbyterian Church of Brazil, several excellent references which were secured, and his work as the Director of MORE International. In that case, we would have clearly stated our reasons for doing so and recorded the ¾ vote of approval by the Presbytery. We acknowledge our error and will be careful in the future to adhere to the BCO 13-6 procedure for examination of those men coming from other denominations NOTE: the man in question is moving to North Carolina where he will continue as Director of MORE International and no doubt seek to be transferred to the Presbytery into whose bounds he moves</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/new-jersey.html">New Jersey</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

Here is the difference, as expressed by the candidate: “ WCF 21.8; WLC 117, 119, WSC 60, 61 regarding recreation and commerce on the Sabbath.</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/nashville.html">Nashville</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> raised (open)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>
<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/pacific-northwest__036.html" data-result-title="Pacific Northwest — 41st (2013) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Pacific Northwest</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>41st (2013)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Pacific Northwest" href="../rpr/exc/pacific-northwest__036.html">Pacific Northwest</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Presbytery granted an exception which appears to be out of accord “that is, hostile to the system or striking at the vitals of religion” ( RAO 16-3.e.5.d), specifically: 27.4 ‘…neither of which may be dispensed by any, but by a minister of the Word lawfully ordained. Perhaps by ‘dispensed’ the Divines refer to the administration and overseeing of the sacramental experiences. However, if they envision that only an ordained minister may handle the elements or the baptismal water, then it seems they create tighter strictures than Scripture itself. For that matter, the proof texts supporting this clause are not compelling. If Matt 28:19 refers only to ordained ministers, then the command to ‘make disciples’ is also limited to ministers. But, of course, the twelve disciples in Matthew represent the new Israel, the re-made people of God whom, corporately, Jesus commissions to extend his kingdom. 1 Cor 11:20, 23 cannot limit the administration to ordained men, since Paul’s point is not to tout his apostolic credentials but simply to recount the transfer of information about the practice of the Lord’s Supper. 1 Cor 4:1 refers to ‘ministers of Christ’ as ‘stewards of the mysteries of God’, but the mysteries are not the sacraments. In the Pauline idiom, the mysteries are the marvelous unfolding of the divine plan to universalize the salvation that had for so long been limited to national Israel. Eph 4:11-12 explains the significance of the offices in the church as ‘for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ’. But these duties are not limited to church officers so much as church officers are specifically tasked with these duties. From these texts anyway, I struggle to support the Confession’s claim about the dispensing of the sacraments.</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/pacific-northwest.html">Pacific Northwest</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>

<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/new-river__086.html" data-result-title="New River — 52nd (2025) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">New River</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>52nd (2025)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="New River" href="../rpr/exc/new-river__086.html">New River</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Presbytery failed to receive a clear statement of a man’s possible difference on the sacraments in his own words.</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/new-river.html">New River</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> raised (open)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>
<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/ohio-valley__037.html" data-result-title="Ohio Valley — 52nd (2025) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Ohio Valley</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>52nd (2025)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Ohio Valley" href="../rpr/exc/ohio-valley__037.html">Ohio Valley</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Presbytery granted a doctrinal exception that appears to be hostile to the system of doctrine or strike at the vitals of religion. In the candidates own words, he says, “As regards who may partake of the Lord’s Supper, I differ with the idea that the New Testament requires covenant children to make a profession of faith (an idea not explicitly stated in the Standards) or mature to the point of self-examination prior to being admitted to the Table. I believe covenant children should be welcomed to the Table of the Lord more or less when they join the table in their homes. Three biblical arguments persuade me of this view: the OT pattern of Passover and other sacrificial feasts, the dubious universalizing of 1 Corinthians 11:28, and the unity of signification between the Sacraments.1 First, it is clear that children partook, and were commanded to partake, of the Passover meal and other sacrificial feasts in the OT (Exod 12:24-27; Deut 12:11-12; 16:10-11), which are forerunners to the Lord’s Supper much as circumcision is to baptism. The unity of the Covenant of Grace is a hallmark of Reformed thought. The Confession says that “The sacraments of the old testament, in regard of the spiritual things thereby signified and exhibited, were, for substance, the same with those of the new” ( WCF 28.5). Given these points, there ought to be a presumption of continuity as to the recipients of the sacraments of nourishment (holy feasts/Lord’s Supper) just as there is for the sacraments of initiation (circumcision/baptism). Second, the chief warrant for seeing discontinuity at this point is Paul’s injunction in 1 Corinthians 11:28: “Let a person examine himself, then, and so eat of the bread and drink of the cup.” It is argued that in this verse Paul issues a universal prerequisite for all worthy partaking in the Lord’s Supper. However, it is dubious whether this verse can be used in this way. The NT letters are occasional documents (1 Corinthians especially so), responding to concrete circumstances in first-century churches. Paul is clear in what he is addressing—exclusionary, factious, and elitist behavior toward fellow church members while ostensibly celebrating the Lord’s Supper (1 Cor 11:18-20). Schismatic behavior that tears at the unity of the body profanes the unity of the bread and the participation in the body of Christ that partaking in the bread signifies (1 Cor 10:14-17). Lots of legitimate application can be made along these lines to the Church today. But to universalize the application of this passage is to take it too far. To deduce from it that Paul intended to set a minimum maturity threshold for participation in the Supper is, in my view, to stretch it beyond the breaking point. Moreover, even if Paul’s injunction to self-examination is taken as broadly as possible, the fact remains that there is a universal injunction to repent and believe prior to baptism for adults which (contrary to Baptists) we do not require of covenant children. Third, Scripture teaches and our Standards affirm that baptism and the Lord’s Supper fundamentally agree in their significance: “the spiritual part of both is Christ and his benefits; both are seals of the same covenant” ( WLC 176). Oddly to my mind, Bavinck, and the Majority Report of the PCA on this subject with him, use this reality to assert the insignificance of withholding the Supper from young children. The children have baptism, the reasoning goes, so it’s not a big deal if they don’t get the Supper yet. But to my mind this point cuts precisely the other way. Since by baptism they already bear Christ’s name, how can they be justly denied his bread? By what token are they granted the one-time sign of union with Christ while being denied the recurring sign of union with Christ? The unity of signification between the Sacraments compels me to think that the reasons for which we baptize our covenant children hold for the question of whether or not to commune our children as well.”</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/ohio-valley.html">Ohio Valley</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> raised (open)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>
<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/pacific-northwest__076.html" data-result-title="Pacific Northwest — 52nd (2025) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Pacific Northwest</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>52nd (2025)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Pacific Northwest" href="../rpr/exc/pacific-northwest__076.html">Pacific Northwest</a><p class="rpr-card__body">g) — No record of requiring statement of differences with our Standards.</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/pacific-northwest.html">Pacific Northwest</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> raised (open)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>
<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/pittsburgh__017.html" data-result-title="Pittsburgh — 52nd (2025) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Pittsburgh</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>52nd (2025)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Pittsburgh" href="../rpr/exc/pittsburgh__017.html">Pittsburgh</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Presbytery judged a stated difference to be “merely semantic,” and that decision needs clarification in light of the candidate’s own words as recorded in the minutes.</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/pittsburgh.html">Pittsburgh</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> satisfactory (closed)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>
<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/platte-valley__016.html" data-result-title="Platte Valley — 52nd (2025) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Platte Valley</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>52nd (2025)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Platte Valley" href="../rpr/exc/platte-valley__016.html">Platte Valley</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Presbytery appears to have incorrectly ruled the following stated difference as merely semantic. Candidate appears to deny the spiritual presence of Christ in the Lord’s Supper, holding only to a memorialist view of the sacrament, which is hostile to our system of doctrine. In candidate’s own words: “I do affirm that by the Spirit, Christ is present in and at the observance of the Supper. I believe that the Spirit does confirm and encourage the faith of those who receive the elements by faith in following Jesus in a unique way. We are to remember with love for Christ and sorrow for our sins his body and blood which were sacrificed for us on the cross. But I cannot say that we feed on his spiritual blood or spiritual body in some literal fashion. The act, both physically and spiritually, occurred once and for all time at Golgotha. We rightly counter Roman Catholics who seem repeatedly to crucify Christ when practicing transubstantiation that turns the bread and wine into the corporeal body and blood to feed upon. I am uncomfortable with the Reformed rite if it turns the bread and wine into his spiritual body and spiritual blood upon which we literally feed. The RCC bodily crucifies Christ again and again through the Mass—or so it appears to many Protestants, myself included. I don’t wish to appear to crucify Christ spiritually again and again through a Lord’s Supper that has recipients eating the spiritual body and spiritual blood. When we “feed on him in our hearts by faith with thanksgiving,” I interpret this to mean that we pause to remember and celebrate that at the cross it was finished both in body and in spirit for our salvation—hallelujah and amen. We figuratively feed upon the accomplished work of Christ at the cross as we apply again and again its saving graces to our daily lives through the agency of the supper when accompanied by faith through the Holy Spirit. Again, I may be misunderstanding what the article is saying, in which case, I welcome conversation, and this might not be an exception. For more see the Larger Catechism 168-170 and the Shorter Catechism 96.”.</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/platte-valley.html">Platte Valley</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> raised (open)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>
<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/rio-grande__061.html" data-result-title="Rio Grande — 52nd (2025) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Rio Grande</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>52nd (2025)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Rio Grande" href="../rpr/exc/rio-grande__061.html">Rio Grande</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Presbytery appears to have incorrectly judged that a candidate’s stated difference is not out of accord with any fundamental of our system of doctrine because the difference is neither hostile to the system nor strikes at the vitals of religion. “4) WLC #177 (maybe WSC #97). I believe in paedocommunion (young child communion). Our baptized children are ‘not only for the solemn admission of the party baptized into the visible Church, but also to be unto him a sign and seal of the covenant of grace, of his ingrafting into Christ, of regeneration, of remission of sins, and of his giving up unto God, through Jesus Christ, to walk in newness of life’ ( WCF 28.1). I believe they should likewise be welcome at the Lord’s Table as part of this family when they are welcomed to the kitchen table as part of their families (i.e., not as suckling infants but as young children). As described in the WCF 31.4, ‘suspension from the sacrament of the Lord’s Supper for a season’ is for those who are being disciplined, and I do not believe it is biblical to treat, our covenant children the same way as 89 ‘obstinate offenders.’ ( WCF 31.3) I agree with Dr. Robert S. Rayburn’s position in the Minority Report to the Ad-Interim Committee to Study the Question of Paedocommunion (16th GA). However, and this is probably the most important aspect of this, i will not nor have i ever practiced anything contrary to that which is permitted in the Westminster Standards and the BCO, as God’s Word and my ordination vows would require me to submit in practice to the judgment of the church in this matter.” [&quot;I believe in paedocommunion.&quot;].</p><span class="home-result__facts"><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Presbytery:</b> <a href="../rpr/rio-grande.html">Rio Grande</a></span><span class="home-result__fact"><b>Final disposition:</b> raised (open)</span></span><details class="result-actions"><summary>Actions</summary><div class="result-actions__panel" aria-label="Record actions"><button type="button" data-result-action="save">Save</button><button type="button" data-result-action="cite">Cite</button><button type="button" data-result-action="link">Copy link</button></div></details></article>
<article class="home-result home-result--rpr rpr-card rpr-card--compact" data-result-item data-result-url="../rpr/exc/rio-grande__062.html" data-result-title="Rio Grande — 52nd (2025) RPR exception" data-result-type="RPR exception"><span class="home-result__metadata"><span class="home-result__category">Rio Grande</span><span class="home-result__separator" aria-hidden="true">•</span><span>52nd (2025)</span></span><a class="home-result__title" data-result-primary data-result-type="RPR exception" data-result-title="Rio Grande" href="../rpr/exc/rio-grande__062.html">Rio Grande</a><p class="rpr-card__body">Presbytery appears to have incorrectly judged that a candidate’s stated difference is not out of accord with any fundamental of our system of doctrine because the difference is neither hostile to the system nor strikes at the vitals of religion. TE seems to imply that making images of God isn’t forbidden by the second commandment. “2) Larger Catechism 109. Where the Confession states ‘The sins forbidden in the second commandment are…the making any representation of God, or of any of the three persons, either inwardly in our mind, or outwardly in any kind of image or likeness of any creature whatsoever,’ I believe that Scripture teaches in the second commandment (Exodus 20:4) that it is forbidden to make idols or images to bow down and worship, but not that it is forbidden to make any representation of God at all, either inwardly or outwardly. Though Christian tradition has generally found it impious to create images of God the Father, it has not generally thought the same with regard to Christ, the Son of God, or the Holy Spirit. More specifically, the Scriptures themselves speak of the form of Jesus (e.g. Isaiah 53, John 20:24- 29, etc.) and of the Holy Spirit in the form of a creature (Matthew 3:16).
